subject: Engelska
title: Grammar: present simple and present continuous
sourceSummary: Present simple for habits and routines, present continuous for something happening right now, and do/does in questions and negative sentences.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "My brother ___ football every Saturday."
questions.opener: Look at "every Saturday" — this is about a habit. Remember what happens to the verb after he/she/it.
questions.explanation: "Every Saturday" shows that it is a habit, so present simple. "My brother" is the same as "he", and then the verb gets -s: "plays". "Play" without -s is used with I/you/we/they.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Be quiet! The baby ___ right now."
questions.opener: "Right now" means something is happening at this very moment.
questions.explanation: Something happening right now is expressed with present continuous: is/am/are + verb with -ing, so "is sleeping". "Sleeps" would mean it is a habit, but "right now" points to this very moment.

questions.opener: Check who is doing the action: should the verb have -s or not?
questions.explanation: With "she" (third person singular), -s is added to the verb in present simple: "She likes pizza". "She like" is one of the very most common mistakes — don't forget -s after he, she and it.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question: "___ your sister play the guitar?"
questions.opener: In present simple questions, do or does is used. Which fits with "your sister"?
questions.explanation: "Your sister" is third person singular (she), so "Does" is used in the question: "Does your sister play...". Note that the main verb stands in its base form without -s once "does" is already in the sentence.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct negative sentence: "He ___ like fish."
questions.opener: In present simple negative sentences, don't or doesn't is used. Which one goes with "he"?
questions.explanation: With he/she/it, "doesn't" + the verb in its base form is used: "He doesn't like fish". "He don't like" is often heard in songs and films, but counts as an error in written English.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that describes a habit, not something happening now.
questions.opener: Habit = present simple. Right now = present continuous. Which sentence describes something that happens every time?
choices: I am watching TV at the moment.
They are eating dinner right now.
We always take the bus to school.
She is doing her homework now.
questions.explanation: "We always take the bus" is present simple with the word "always" — it describes a habit. The other sentences have is/am/are + -ing together with "now" or "at the moment", which means something is happening right now.

questions.prompt: Correct the three errors: "My friend live in London. Right now he watch TV. He don't like sport."
questions.opener: Look for three things: -s in the third person, the tense with "right now", and the correct negative form.
questions.answer: My friend lives in London. Right now he is watching TV. He doesn't like sport.
steps: "My friend live" → "My friend lives". "My friend" is the same as "he", so the verb gets -s in present simple.
"Right now he watch TV" → "Right now he is watching TV". "Right now" means it is ongoing, so we use present continuous: is + watching.
"He don't like" → "He doesn't like". With he/she/it, doesn't is used, not don't.
After "doesn't", the verb stands in its base form: "like", never "likes".

questions.prompt: When do you use present simple and when do you use present continuous?
questions.opener: Two tenses, two situations — plus the rules for -s and do/does.
questions.answer: Present simple = habits and things that are always true (I play football every week) · he/she/it gets -s: he plays, she watches · questions: Do you play? / Does he play? · negative: I don't play / He doesn't play · after do/does the verb stands in its base form. Present continuous = something happening right now (I am playing right now) · formed with am/is/are + verb-ing · signal words: now, right now, at the moment, look!, listen! · signal words for present simple: always, usually, often, sometimes, never, every day.
